script: I tried a million random networks on this spiral. The best one gets 69 percent right.
Same network as the backpropagation video: a hundred and five numbers. Each try picks all of them at random, and counts how many of the four hundred points it gets right.
Ten tries: 58 percent. A thousand: 64. A hundred thousand: 69. Then nothing. Not one better network in the last 941 thousand.
Now gradient descent. One random start, and at every step, it follows the slope that backpropagation computes.
Step 94: it already beats the best of the million. Step fifteen hundred: ninety-five and a half percent.
And it needed about three thousand runs of the network. The random search used a million.
Guessing can't work. Even ten choices for each of the hundred and five numbers makes ten to the power of a hundred and five networks. The universe has about ten to the eighty atoms.
The slope says which way to move every number, all at once. That's what backpropagation buys you.
